{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Amanda, it looks like you've been experiencing a lot lately. How are you holding up?
seeker: Hi, yeah, it's been a bit rough. Work is really getting to me right now.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it your supervisor again?
seeker: Yes, exactly. I just feel like no matter how hard I try, my efforts aren't valued.
supporter: That sounds incredibly frustrating. It's understandable to feel that way when you're working so hard. What happened recently that's making it worse?
seeker: Yesterday, I suggested a new project plan, but he just dismissed it without even giving it a second thought. I felt humiliated in front of my team.
supporter: That must have been so discouraging. Knowing that this has been an ongoing issue, how are you coping with the stress?
seeker: I'm trying to stay focused on the projects and find satisfaction in my work itself, but it's tough.
supporter: It's admirable that you're trying to find inner satisfaction. Have you been able to talk about this with anyone else at work, maybe someone who could support your ideas?
seeker: I talked with a coworker who apologized for past issues a while ago. They seem supportive, but there's only so much they can do.
supporter: It's good to have even a little bit of support. Have you considered any strategies to improve the situation with your supervisor?
seeker: I've thought about it, but honestly, I feel stuck. I want to have an open dialogue, but every time I try, it backfires.
supporter: That sounds incredibly challenging. It seems like you're stuck between a rock and a hard place. How can I support you through this?
seeker: I think just talking about it helps. Sometimes I feel so alone in this, and it's reassuring to have someone listen.
supporter: I'm here anytime you need to talk. You're definitely not alone, and what you're feeling is completely valid.
seeker: Thanks, that really means a lot. I think I've also been emotionally drained since my breakup last month.
supporter: Breakups are incredibly tough, especially on top of everything else. Have you been able to find some personal time to process everything?
seeker: I've been trying to, but between work stress and personal life, it's been challenging to find time for myself.
supporter: It's important to carve out some 'you' time whenever you can. Perhaps it might help to set small boundaries, even if just for a moment of calm.
seeker: That's a good idea, actually. Maybe a short walk during lunch or some time reading a book could work.
supporter: That sounds perfect. Even small steps like that can make a huge difference in how you feel.
seeker: I'll try to make it a habit. I need something positive to focus on.
supporter: That's the spirit. Remember, I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're doing the best you can, and that's more than enough.
seeker: Thank you so much. Having someone to talk to really helps keep me grounded.
supporter: You're very welcome. Anytime you need me, just reach out. You've got this, Amanda.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-11-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: hi there
supporter: Hello! How are you doing? 
seeker: I'm not doing so good at the moment. I'm feeling very stressed and burned out from work
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. Is this a recent development at your job? 
seeker: It's been building up for a while now, but it's really starting to get a but overwhelming
supporter: I can understand how that can have an effect on your mental well-being. Have you spoken to your supervisor about your frustrations at work? 
seeker: I have, but sometimes I feel like she doesn't really listen and she sort of talks over me a lot
supporter: It sounds like you don't feel listened to. 
seeker: That's right... I guess that is quite a lot of the problem. 
seeker: I don't mind so much the work, I know it is busy for everyone right now, it's a combination of the workload plus not being listened to
supporter: I had a similar issue at my last job. My supervisor constantly spoke over me in meetings, and it would drive me crazy. I never could get a word in edge-wise. 
seeker: Yeah, that sounds a lot like what I am experiencing
supporter: Are you considering switching jobs? 
seeker: It's been in the back of my mind, but it's a hard time just now with everything else going on
supporter: Absolutely. It's a rough time job searching under the best of circumstances. 
seeker: It is. 
supporter: Have you tried reaching out to anyone in your network to look for a new position? It helped me when I was previously job searching. 
seeker: I haven't, but it might be worth getting in touch with some people
supporter: Absolutely. I also spoke with a therapist before and it helped me a lot. 
supporter: Have you considered reaching out to a professional to talk to? 
seeker: I did consider that, but aren't they expensive?
supporter: They can be, but many local governments and municipalities have therapists that work on a sliding scale if the financial aspect of therapy is a concern. 
supporter: Therapy can definitely be a large expense though. 
seeker: It might be worth it in the long run though I guess, if it helps how I am feeling
supporter: If it helps to reframe the expense, you can try to think of it as an investment in your mental health. 
seeker: Yes, that sounds like a more positive way of thinking of it
supporter: The therapist could likely give you some tools to help manage the frustrations at your workplace more constructively. 
seeker: Yes, I imagine they will have come across this before so will be able to help
supporter: Absolutely. I hope that you're able to find some peace at your workplace with your boss. 
seeker: Thank you, you have helped a lot
seeker: Helped give me some ideas to try to help
supporter: It's my pleasure. I'm happy to have helped you. 
supporter: Is there anything else I can help you with? ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Amanda, how have you been holding up lately?
seeker: Hi, honestly, it's been a tough couple of days. I finally had the big talk with Bill, and we decided to break up.
supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like a really difficult decision to come to. Do you want to talk about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it's just... we've been together for three years, but we've been stuck on what our future looks like. Our life goals just don't align anymore.
supporter: That must be so hard, especially after investing so much time and emotion into the relationship. How are you feeling about it all?
seeker: A mix of emotions, really. I feel sad and a little lost. But there's also relief, you know? Like, at least now I can move forward instead of being in limbo.
supporter: It's understandable to feel conflicted. Breakups can bring about such a wide range of emotions. It's good you're finding some silver lining in it.
seeker: Yeah, it's just that I thought we were going to build a life together, and now it's like I have to start over in a way.
supporter: It definitely feels overwhelming having to rethink your future plans. Do you feel like talking to your relatives again has given you any support?
seeker: Actually, yes. Since I reconnected with my family at my aunt's memorial, they've been really supportive. It's nice to know they're there for me.
supporter: That's so important, having a support system to lean on. Have you spoken to any of your friends or coworkers about it?
seeker: I told a few friends, and they've been great. Work's been a distraction, and ever since my coworker and I made up, it's been a more positive environment.
supporter: It sounds like you're doing a great job surrounding yourself with positive energy and support. What about self-care? Are you finding time for yourself?
seeker: I'm trying to. I watched a favorite movie and went for a long walk yesterday to clear my head. It's the little things, I guess.
supporter: Definitely, those small acts of self-care can make such a big difference. What do you feel like you need most right now?
seeker: I think I just need time to process everything, to let myself feel and heal without rushing into anything new.
supporter: Taking the time you need is so important. Give yourself grace, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need someone to talk to.
seeker: Thank you, that means a lot. I'll definitely keep that in mind.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
seeker: I am feeling angry today about work. 
supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me. 
supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her. 
supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way. 
supporter: I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
seeker: Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other. 
supporter: Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
supporter: She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.
seeker: That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping. 
supporter: I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block.  And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Then you can lay out how you work best and see where it goes from there.
seeker: Thanks! I will try that. You made me feel so much better! 
supporter: I'm so glad, these can be frustrating situations but sometimes it's worth looking at the other person's perspective.
seeker: I agree. Sometimes you just have to take a step back and have a conversation with someone not in the thick of it. 
supporter: Absolutely, I have no emotional stake in this. The two of you do and that can cloud things sometimes.
seeker: I think people get territorial when they have worked somewhere and a new person comes in. I see that now. I am optimistic we will work it out and be a great team!
supporter: That's great to hear, I'm glad we were able to chat!
seeker: Me too! You really helped me. Have a wonderful day! I know I will since you helped me out. 
supporter: That's great, good luck!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

supporter: Can you identify why you feel sad?
seeker: yes, my aunt pass away a couple weeks ago
seeker: and since then im feeling really sad

seeker: No, I live alone, my family lives in another state
supporter: Being by yourself is rough after a death.    Can you talk with your family by phone?   Do you have a friend who has gone through a similar loss?
seeker: I feel like everybody is in their own bussines and have no time to hear my complains

supporter: It sounds like you feel people think you are complaining when you talk about your Aunt's death making you sad.    Is that correct?

memory.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
supporter: That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
seeker: It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
seeker: Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
supporter: That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
seeker: I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
supporter: That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
seeker: A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
seeker: You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
supporter: That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?
seeker: I'm thinking of arranging a small family gathering, something more joy-filled, to keep everyone in touch.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.
seeker: I hope so. It feels good just talking about it. Thanks for listening and helping me work through this.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

turns.content: Hi, I really need to talk about something that's been weighing on me recently.
Of course, Amanda. I'm here for you. What's going on?
I received another negative performance review from my supervisor, and it's really getting to me.
I'm so sorry to hear that. How are you feeling about the review?
It's just so frustrating. I feel like no matter how hard I work, it's never enough.
That's really tough. It sounds like you're putting in so much effort and not getting the recognition you deserve.
Exactly. It's not just this review; it's been a pattern with my supervisor for a while now.
That's understandable. It must be incredibly discouraging to face that repeatedly.
Yes, and it's starting to affect my motivation. I feel so undervalued.
Feeling undervalued at work can be so draining. Do you have any support or allies in the workplace that you can talk to about this?
I've mended things with a coworker recently, which has helped a bit. But it's still so lonely dealing with this.
I'm glad to hear that you have someone you can at least partially lean on. Have you thought about addressing this with anyone higher up or in HR?
I have, but I'm worried it might make things worse with my supervisor if they find out.
That's a valid concern. It's important to weigh the potential outcomes. How are you handling the stress outside of work?
Honestly, not well. The stress is impacting my personal life too, especially after my recent breakup.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate all at once. It must be hard to find peace right now.
It is. I'm trying to stay connected with family, but I still feel quite lost.
Reconnecting with family after the memorial service was a positive step. It’s okay to lean on them for support in times like these.
You're right. I need to reach out more, even though it's hard.
